newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Opposition strike disrupts life in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Opposition strike disrupts life in Bangladesh.

text.p: Riot police and para-military forces on Sunday patroled streets and guarded key public installations as an opposition-led strike virtually halted life across Bangladesh, witnesses said.
The strike, called by the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, shut businesses and kept traffic off the roads.
The witnesses said hundreds of government employees either walked to work or took pedal rickshaws, defying the strike call. Many top government officials stayed in their offices overnight.
Sunday is a working day in mainly Moslem Bangladesh.
Police said the strike had been peaceful so far except for the detonations of a few home-made bombs early in the morning heralding the start of the eight-hour stoppage. No casulaties were reported.
The BNP called the strike as its first major offensive in a campaign to destabilise the eight-month-old government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

Hasina took office last June after defeating the BNP in a general election in which both the BNP and Hasina's Awami League accused each other of vote-rigging, but which was billed as free and fair by local and international monitors.

The BNP says the strike is intended as a protest against what it views as the government's failure to provide for the basic needs of citizens in this poor nation and against Hasina's warmer ties with rival India, which the BNP sees as a plot to surrender Bangladeshi sovereignty.
